What a Barn Find: 1968 Mustang California Special Saved After 41 Years, Needs Restoration
41 photos
Photo: eBay seller kikiann727
Barn finds are the best finds, and this 1968 Ford Mustang California Special GT/CS is here to prove this to the world. The car spent the last 41 years locked in a barn, and despite this super-long tenure away from the road, it’s still in good shape.
The reason why it is here is pretty simple: the man who saved the car is now willing to let it go, so someone else can restore this fairly rare Mustang .
The GT/CS came to be at the San Jose plant only, and Ford produced only 4,118 units. The demand for this special model was impressive, but due to various production challenges, the output ended up quite limited. This is why the California Special is a highly desirable model these days, especially in collector circles where all-original models are particularly sought-after.
The California Special came with 1965 T-Bird taillights, fiberglass trunk lid, quarter extensions, side scoops, fog lights, a blacked-out front grille, and an exclusive coupe body style.
This specimen still appears to have all of these, so most likely, the owners locked the car in the barn and never turned it into a donor for other projects. This was undoubtedly the right choice, as the Mustang now appears to be complete and in good shape for restoration. It still has the fiberglass goodies, though I think that anyone interested in a purchase should call the seller and discuss how they can see the car in person.
This is a barn find that’s been sitting for over 4 days, so a live inspection should come in very handy. The engine under the hood isn’t the best, but it’s not the worst either. The GT/CS could be ordered with any engine in the lineup, but the buyer of this specimen picked a 289 V8 paired with an automatic transmission. The engine turns over, and the seller says they did not work on it, meaning that you’ll be the one who takes care of the rest.
The engine should still be in good shape, considering it turns over, but a good mechanic should be able to decrypt additional information quite easily.
The owner looks fully committed to letting this Mustang go, so they posted the car on eBay without a reserve. This means that the highest bidder is free to take the car home when the battle ends in 3 days and a few more hours. The top bid at the time of writing is $8,600, but the battle could soon get a lot fiercer, considering the vehicle ended up on the watchlist of no more, no less than 181 people.
Bidders often submit an offer at the very last minute, so be prepared for a difficult race to get your hands on this car. It’s parked in Webster, New York.
